- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.3) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) in recent days, model tends to underestimate; increase forecast modestly to capture mean reversion.
- Model often overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., 73+), leading to over-forecasted peaks; apply a lagged smoothing or cap at +5% above recent high.
- In low-sentiment periods (sentiment near 0), model shows persistent bias toward recent mean; adjust by adding 1–2% upward bias to counteract mean reversion.
- Forecast horizon 30d often exhibits “late correction” bias — true values tend to be higher than forecasted in the final 5–7 days; increase final 5–7 day forecast by 1–3% to align with observed trend persistence.
- When sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., +0.3 → -0.4 → +0.2), model fails to capture volatility; reduce forecast volatility by 10–20% in such regimes.
